entry.display: AOSpine thoracolumbar injury classification (2013 consensus paper)
entry.issuer: AOSpine Spinal Cord Injury & Trauma Knowledge Forum (Vaccaro AR et al.)
entry.purpose: Classifies an acute thoracolumbar spine injury by fracture morphology, with neurological status and case-specific modifiers, in spinal trauma; designed mainly around features seen on CT. Not for chronic fractures or low-energy osteoporotic insufficiency fractures.

locator.section: Results: Type A Injuries (journal p2030-2031)

definitions.text: Type A: compression injury of the vertebral body (anterior elements, vertebral body and/or disc) with the tension band intact and no translation; may be an isolated single-vertebra injury or occur with type B or C injuries.

locator.section: Results: Type A Injuries (journal p2030-2031)

definitions.text: A0: no vertebral fracture, or a clinically insignificant fracture such as of a spinous or transverse process; no concern for mechanical instability or neurological deficit.

locator.section: Results: Type A Injuries (journal p2030-2031)

definitions.text: A1: wedge compression or impaction fracture of a single endplate, without involvement of the posterior wall of the vertebral body; the vertebral canal is intact.

locator.section: Results: Type A Injuries (journal p2030-2031)

definitions.text: A2: split or pincer-type fracture with the fracture line through both endplates, without involvement of the posterior vertebral wall.

locator.section: Results: Type A Injuries (journal p2030-2031); Figure 6 legend

definitions.text: A3: incomplete burst, a vertebral fracture of a single endplate with any involvement of the posterior vertebral wall and the spinal canal. A vertical lamina fracture is usually present and does not indicate tension band failure.

locator.section: Results: Type A Injuries (journal p2030-2031); Figure 7 legend

definitions.text: A4: complete burst, a vertebral body fracture of both endplates with any involvement of the posterior wall; split fractures that also involve the posterior wall are included. A vertical lamina fracture does not indicate tension band failure.

locator.section: Results: Type B Injuries: Tension Band Injury (journal p2032-2033)

definitions.text: Type B: failure of the posterior or anterior tension band without gross translation or the potential for gross translation; may be seen with a type A vertebral body fracture.

locator.section: Results: Type B Injuries: Tension Band Injury (journal p2032-2033)

definitions.text: B1: monosegmental osseous (transosseous) failure of the posterior tension band extending into the vertebral body, the classical 'chance' fracture; it affects a single vertebral level.

locator.section: Results: Type B Injuries: Tension Band Injury (journal p2032-2033)

definitions.text: B2: disruption of the posterior tension band, bony and/or ligamentous, always at an intervertebral level; any associated vertebral body fracture is specified separately by its type A subtype.

locator.section: Results: Type B Injuries: Tension Band Injury (journal p2032-2033)

definitions.text: B3: disruption of the anterior longitudinal ligament (the anterior tension band) through the disc or the vertebral body, with an intact posterior element hinge that prevents gross displacement; typically a hyperextension injury, notably in ankylosed spines.

locator.section: Results: Type C Injuries: Displacement/Translational Injury (journal p2033)

definitions.text: Type C: displacement beyond the physiological range of the cranial and caudal parts of the spinal column in any plane, or distraction of anterior and posterior elements with no intact structure remaining, or complete disruption of the posterior hinge even without translation. No subtypes.

locator.section: Results: Grading of Injuries (journal p2030-2031)

definitions.text: Coding by level: A and B1 injuries are coded by the single vertebral level (e.g. L2); B2, B3 and C injuries affect a motion segment and are coded by it (e.g. T12-L1). The colloquial term (burst, chance, etc.) may follow the alphanumeric code.

locator.section: Results: Grading of Injuries (journal p2030-2031)

definitions.text: Multilevel injuries are classified separately and listed in declining severity; injuries of the same subtype are listed from cranial to caudal.

locator.section: Results: Grading of Neurological Deficits (journal p2033-2034)

definitions.text: N0: neurologically intact.

locator.section: Results: Grading of Neurological Deficits (journal p2033-2034)

definitions.text: N1: transient neurological deficit, no longer present.

locator.section: Results: Grading of Neurological Deficits (journal p2033-2034)

definitions.text: N2: symptoms or signs of radiculopathy.

locator.section: Results: Grading of Neurological Deficits (journal p2033-2034)

definitions.text: N3: incomplete spinal cord injury, or cauda equina injury.

locator.section: Results: Grading of Neurological Deficits (journal p2033-2034)

definitions.text: N4: complete spinal cord injury (American Spinal Injury Association grade A).

locator.section: Results: Grading of Neurological Deficits (journal p2033-2034)

definitions.text: NX: patient who cannot be examined (head injury, intoxication, multiple trauma, intubation or sedation, or another condition preventing a neurological examination).

locator.section: Results: Case-Specific Modifiers (journal p2034)

definitions.text: M1: fracture that seems stable from a bony standpoint but has an indeterminate injury to the tension band on spinal imaging such as MRI, or on clinical examination; the source says ligamentous insufficiency may then help decide whether operative stabilization is considered.

locator.section: Results: Case-Specific Modifiers (journal p2034)

definitions.text: M2: a patient-specific comorbidity that might argue for or against surgery where there are relative indications; examples include ankylosing spondylitis, rheumatological conditions, DISH, osteopenia or osteoporosis, or burns over the injured spine.

locator.section: Conclusion (journal p2036); Spine Injury Score (journal p2034)

pitfalls.text: The paper gives no treatment rule or score per grade, and the Spine Injury Score it mentions is not defined. The authors only state expectations (M1 to give greater consideration to surgery; C injuries and extension-distraction injuries in an ankylosed spine expected to need stabilization). A grade should not be turned into a recommendation from this source.

locator.section: Results: Type A Injuries (journal p2030-2031); Results: Type B Injuries: Tension Band Injury (journal p2032-2033)

pitfalls.text: A3 or A4 morphology with ligamentous disruption of the posterior tension band is primarily classified B2, with the A3 or A4 body injury specified separately. A3 or A4 with a horizontal axial-plane fracture through the posterior elements is a type B injury.

locator.section: Results: Type A Injuries (journal p2030-2031); Figures 6 and 7 legends

pitfalls.text: A vertical (greenstick-like) lamina fracture with a burst fracture does not by itself indicate tension band failure.

locator.section: Results: Type B Injuries: Tension Band Injury (journal p2032-2033); Results: Type C Injuries: Displacement/Translational Injury (journal p2033); Discussion (journal p2036)

pitfalls.text: If the posterior hinge is clearly and completely disrupted, the injury is type C with a B descriptor even without displacement at the time of injury. An extension injury in an ankylosed spine without displacement was graded B3 by some observers and C by others.

locator.section: Results: Type B Injuries: Tension Band Injury (journal p2032-2033); Figure 9 legend; Results: Type C Injuries: Displacement/Translational Injury (journal p2033)

pitfalls.text: With a type B injury, an associated vertebral body fracture is specified separately by its type A subtype (e.g. T12-L1 B2 with T12 A4). With a type C injury, an associated body fracture and, if possible, any associated tension band injury (B1 to B3) are specified separately.

locator.section: Results: Interobserver Reliability (journal p2035); Discussion (journal p2036)

pitfalls.text: B2 and B3 had the lowest subtype agreement (kappa 0.34 and 0.41), and the authors note that MRI identification of posterior ligamentous complex injury is poorly reliable. B1 versus B2 depends on a ligamentous component and may not be easy to make.

locator.section: Materials and Methods (journal p2029)

pitfalls.text: The paper classifies the thoracolumbar spine only; the upper cervical, lower cervical and sacral regions are described separately and are not covered here.

locator.section: Conclusion (journal p2036)

pitfalls.text: This is the consensus paper with a 40-case reliability study (level of evidence 4); the authors state that broad prospective validation is still needed before it informs surgical decision making.

locator.section: Results: opening list of 3 basic parameters (journal p2030)

summary.text: The system describes a thoracolumbar injury with three parts: a morphologic type (A, B or C, with subtypes), a neurological status (N0 to N4, or NX) and, only when relevant, case-specific modifiers (M1, M2).

locator.section: Results: Morphologic Classification (journal p2030)

summary.text: Morphology is graded by the mode of failure of the spinal column: A compression, B failure of the posterior or anterior tension band without gross translation, C failure of all elements with displacement. Successive types indicate ascending severity.

locator.section: Discussion (journal p2035-2036)

summary.text: The scheme is built around features seen on CT. MRI may show tension band disruption (making the injury at least type B) or a disrupted posterior hinge (making an extension-distraction injury type C); the authors note poor reliability of MRI for posterior ligamentous complex injury.

locator.section: Conclusion (journal p2036); also Spine Injury Score (journal p2034)

summary.text: The paper gives no treatment rule or score per grade. The Spine Injury Score is left to be developed, and the authors state that no absolute recommendations on when surgery is mandatory can be given. Attributed expectations: M1 is meant to give greater consideration to surgery when the posterior ligamentous complex is indeterminate; an extension injury in an ankylosed spine is highly unstable; type C injuries and extension-distraction injuries in an ankylosed spine would mostly be expected to be treated with surgical stabilization.

locator.section: Results: Final Evaluation Session; Interobserver Reliability (journal p2034)

summary.text: Reliability was tested on 40 cases graded by 9 spine surgeons: interobserver kappa 0.72 for injury type (A/B/C) and 0.64 overall including subtypes (level of evidence 4). The authors call for prospective validation.

entry.purpose: Scores early ischaemic change in the middle cerebral artery territory on non-contrast CT in hyperacute ischaemic stroke, as part of the pre-treatment CT assessment before thrombolysis.

pitfalls.text: Cohort: 156 patients treated with intravenous alteplase alone within 3 hours of stroke onset at two North American hospitals, March 1996 to May 1999; non-contrast CT on 10 mm slices. It predates thrombectomy; the figures are not for patients considered for thrombectomy or any other treatment.

locator.section: Methods, Patients: only patients thought to have anterior-circulation ischaemia were included in the analysis (journal p1670-1671); Results: 23 patients with posterior-circulation ischaemia were not analysed (p1672)

pitfalls.text: ASPECTS was derived and tested in anterior-circulation (MCA territory) ischaemia; 23 posterior-circulation patients were not analysed. It is not pc-ASPECTS, which is a different posterior-circulation score not covered by this source.

locator.section: Methods, Procedures: ASPECTS allots the middle-cerebral-artery territory 10 points; one point is subtracted for early ischaemic change in each defined region; a normal CT scores 10 and 0 indicates diffuse ischaemia throughout the territory (journal p1671)

pitfalls.text: A score of 10 means no early ischaemic change in the ten MCA regions only; it does not exclude haemorrhage, an old infarct, or ischaemia outside the MCA territory.

locator.section: Discussion (journal p1673)

pitfalls.text: The odds ratio of 14 for symptomatic haemorrhage rests on 10 events in total (95% CI 1.8 to 117; the text gives 2 to 117). The 1% rate above 7 is 1 of 91, slightly above the 0.6% on placebo in the NINDS trial.

locator.section: Statistics (journal p1671)

pitfalls.text: The cut-off of 7 or less versus above 7 was suggested by a review of the study data, not set in advance.

locator.section: Discussion (journal p1673)

pitfalls.text: Study limitation: it could not show how patients scoring 7 or less would have fared without treatment, and the authors called for validation in a randomised controlled study.

locator.section: Methods, Procedures: ASPECTS allots the middle-cerebral-artery territory 10 points; one point is subtracted for early ischaemic change in each defined region; a normal CT scores 10 and 0 indicates diffuse ischaemia throughout the territory (journal p1671)

pitfalls.text: Agreement between observers for 7 or less versus above 7 was poorer without knowledge of the affected side (kappa 0.39 to 0.69) than with it (0.71 to 0.89).

Code the most suspicious protrusion: an enhancing one over a non-enhancing one, and a nodule over irregular thickening.

locator.section: Chapter 4 introduction

definitions.text: A thyroid nodule on ultrasound is a discrete lesion that can be told apart from the adjacent normal thyroid parenchyma.
Taller than wide: the anteroposterior diameter exceeds the transverse diameter (AP > TR) in the axial plane.
Spongiform (honeycomb): microcystic spaces with thin walls making up more than half of the nodule.

locator.section: 4.3 Selection of nodules for FNAC

definitions.text: In a mixed solid and cystic nodule, assess the solid part: an eccentric solid portion, a non-smooth margin, hypoechogenicity and microcalcification within it are specific signs of malignancy; a taller-than-wide or irregular overall shape also predicts malignancy.

locator.section: Abstract; 1. Introduction

summary.text: CAC-DRS is the SCCT 2018 consensus reporting system for coronary artery calcium on non-contrast CT. It applies to all dedicated CAC scans and to all non-gated non-contrast chest CT, irrespective of the indication, and gives one category from 0 to 3 per patient with a risk statement.

locator.section: 3.1, 3.2; 4.1 Scoring system

summary.text: The category comes from the total Agatston score, or from a visual none/mild/moderate/severe estimate on non-gated scans. The category carries the same meaning either way, but the scoring system used should be documented.

locator.section: 4.2 Number of involved vessels

summary.text: Two modifiers are reported: A (Agatston) or V (visual), and N, the number of vessels with calcium (1 to 4). N is prognostically additive to the total score, but data are insufficient to change the category on it; it may influence how aggressively management is pursued. N is not used for category 0.

definitions.text: Stenosis grading: 0% no visible stenosis; 1-24% minimal; 25-49% mild; 50-69% moderate; 70-99% severe; 100% occluded.
CAD-RADS 4 is split: 4A is a 70-99% stenosis; 4B is left main stenosis ≥50% or three-vessel obstructive (≥70%) disease.
Plaque burden P1 mild, P2 moderate, P3 severe, P4 extensive; by CAC 1-100, 101-300, 301-999, >1000, or by segment involvement score ≤2, 3-4, 5-7, ≥8, or visually. P is not used with CAD-RADS 0.

Modifier I records a CT ischaemia test (CT-FFR or stress CTP): I+ lesion-specific ischaemia, a reversible perfusion defect or peri-infarct ischaemia (stress defect larger than rest defect); I- negative, including a fixed infarct without ischaemia; I+/- borderline.

definitions.text: Adrenal incidentaloma: an adrenal mass found on imaging not done for suspected adrenal disease. Masses found on hereditary-syndrome screening or cancer staging fall outside the strict definition; work-up applies from 1 cm.

definitions.text: Relative washout = 100 x (HUmax - HU10/15min) / HUmax; absolute washout = 100 x (HUmax - HU10/15min) / (HUmax - HUunenhanced), from unenhanced, 60-second and 10 or 15 minute delayed phases.

pitfalls.text: Not for adrenal masses found at staging or follow-up of a known extra-adrenal malignancy (ESE's separate pathway, Figure 9), on imaging for suspected adrenal disease, or on hereditary-syndrome screening.

Heterogeneous masses should not go on to MRI or washout CT for characterisation; Table 4 criteria apply only to homogeneous masses or clear benign entities such as myelolipoma.
The 58% relative washout cut-off rests on a single study of 253 tumours and should be used with caution; older studies suggest 40%.
With bilateral or multiple adrenal masses, assess each lesion separately by the same imaging protocol; review the contralateral adrenal, which is often also hyperplastic or nodular.

entry.purpose: Gives follow-up recommendations for solid and subsolid pulmonary nodules found incidentally on CT in adults; not intended for lung cancer screening.

locator.section: General Recommendations

definitions.text: Size is the average of the long- and short-axis diameters, measured on the same image (transverse, coronal or sagittal) showing the largest dimensions, rounded to the nearest millimetre. <6 mm means a rounded size of 5 mm or less.

locator.section: Risk Estimation and Risk Models

definitions.text: Low risk is an estimated cancer risk below 5% (younger age, less smoking, smaller size, regular margins, non-upper-lobe). High risk combines the ACCP intermediate (5–65%) and high (>65%) categories.

locator.section: Tobacco and Other Inhaled Carcinogens; Risk Estimation and Risk Models

definitions.text: High-risk factors include older age, heavy smoking (30 pack-years or more and quitting within the past 15 years, the NLST threshold), larger size, irregular or spiculated margins and upper lobe location.

locator.section: Nodule Size and Morphology

definitions.text: Subsolid nodules are ground-glass (no solid component) or part-solid. Components visible on mediastinal (soft-tissue) window settings are solid.

locator.section: Recommendation 2: multiple solid noncalcified nodules

definitions.text: With multiple nodules, the most suspicious (dominant) nodule guides management; it may not be the largest. The others are monitored on follow-up.

locator.section: Tobacco and Other Inhaled Carcinogens

definitions.text: Subsolid nodule recommendations do not depend on the customary risk categories.

locator.section: Table note; Introduction and Implications for Patient Care (p. 2)

pitfalls.text: Does not apply to lung cancer screening (use Lung-RADS), patients under 35, immunocompromised patients or patients with known primary cancer.

locator.section: General Recommendations

pitfalls.text: Volumetric thresholds (100 and 250 mm³) are given by the source but are not supported here yet; enter the average diameter.

locator.section: Figures 1 and 2

pitfalls.text: Applies to noncalcified nodules. Benign calcification patterns or fat (e.g. hamartoma, granuloma) need no CT follow-up.

locator.section: Perifissural Nodules

pitfalls.text: Perifissural or juxtapleural nodules with typical lymph node morphology need no follow-up, even above 6 mm; spiculation, fissure displacement or cancer history change this.

locator.section: Recommendation 4: solitary part-solid lung nodules

pitfalls.text: For part-solid nodules, the table size is the whole nodule; a solid component of 6 mm or more, or above 8 mm, changes management.

locator.section: Recommendation 2: multiple solid noncalcified nodules

pitfalls.text: The table has no row for a mix of solid and subsolid nodules; the source says the most suspicious nodule guides management.

locator.section: Incidentally Detected Lung Nodules on Incomplete Thoracic CT Scans

pitfalls.text: Nodules on partial chest CT (e.g. abdomen): <6 mm need no further imaging; 6–8 mm need complete chest CT at 3–12 months.

locator.section: General Recommendations

pitfalls.text: If the first scan used thick sections, a short-term thin-section follow-up may be needed before applying the table.

summary.text: Fleischner Society 2017 guidance for incidental pulmonary nodules on CT in adults aged 35 or over, revising the earlier Fleischner guidelines for solid and subsolid nodules.
Management is set by nodule type (solid, ground-glass, part-solid), single or multiple, size, and for solid nodules the patient's clinical risk.

locator.section: Advances in Knowledge

summary.text: The threshold for routine follow-up of solid nodules is 6 mm; subsolid nodules are followed longer, up to 5 years.
Ranges of follow-up intervals are deliberate, leaving room for radiologist, clinician and patient preference.

entry.issuer: Garden RS (Preston Royal Infirmary)
entry.purpose: Classifies a subcapital (intracapsular) femoral neck fracture into stages by its degree of displacement on radiographs taken before reduction.

locator.section: Figure 6 caption

definitions.text: Stage I, incomplete subcapital fracture: the abducted or impacted injury. The inferior cortical buttress has a greenstick break and slight lateral rotation of the distal fragment gives the look of impaction. The medial trabeculae of the distal fragment lie in abduction relative to those of the adducted capital fragment. Left unprotected it may become complete.

locator.section: Figure 7 caption

definitions.text: Stage II, complete subcapital fracture without displacement: the inferior cortical buttress is broken but the capital fragment has not tilted. The closely opposed fragments may still displace under lateral rotation forces.

locator.section: Figure 8 caption

definitions.text: Stage III, complete subcapital fracture with partial displacement: the fragments keep their posterior retinacular attachment and the posterior cervical cortex is not yet crushed. Lateral rotation of the distal fragment tilts the capital fragment into abduction and medial rotation, shown by the direction of the medial trabeculae in the head.

locator.section: Figure 9 caption

definitions.text: Stage IV, complete subcapital fracture with full displacement: the retinacular hinge is detached from the back of the neck and the posterior cortical shell has collapsed. The fragments are separated and the capital fragment returns to a more normal position in the acetabulum, its medial trabeculae in line with those of the pelvis.

locator.section: Classification

definitions.text: Intermediary types between the stages may sometimes be recognised. The paper does not describe them or say how to name them.

locator.section: Classification

definitions.text: The stage describes the radiographic appearance before reduction. The paper uses 'Stage I to IV' and does not itself call them Garden grades or types.

locator.section: Classification pp.653-654

pitfalls.text: The paper defines the stages only for subcapital fractures of the femoral neck. It does not apply them to extracapsular (intertrochanteric or pertrochanteric), mid-cervical or basal fractures.

locator.section: Reduction (stage-by-stage remarks), PDF pp.9-10

pitfalls.text: The paper gives no management recommendation and no outcome or prognosis data per stage. Its remarks on reduction at each stage (for example, reduction at Stage III is easy and stable, and Stage IV often defies closed and open reduction) are the author's operative comments for low-angle nailing in 1961, not recommendations to report.

locator.section: Classification

pitfalls.text: The paper does not group stages into undisplaced (I and II) and displaced (III and IV) and does not give numeric limits for partial or full displacement. Any such grouping is later usage, not part of this card.

locator.section: Summary and Conclusions

pitfalls.text: The classification was proposed on the author's own series, and the paper reports no observer agreement for the stages. His caveat that publication was premature concerns the low-angle fixation results, not the classification itself.

locator.section: Avascular necrosis p.662; Reduction p.654; Summary p.17

pitfalls.text: The alignment index (about 160 degrees in the frontal and 180 degrees in the lateral view) and the avascular-necrosis and union data in the paper concern the quality of reduction in his series, not the Garden stage. Do not read them as a prognosis per stage.

locator.section: Figure 9 caption

pitfalls.text: At Stage IV the capital fragment can sit in a near-normal position with its trabeculae aligned with the pelvis, so a well-aligned head alone does not mean the fracture is undisplaced.

locator.section: Classification

summary.text: Garden described four stages of subcapital femoral neck fracture by how far the fragments are displaced before reduction: incomplete (I), complete without displacement (II), complete with partial displacement (III) and complete with full displacement (IV).

locator.section: Classification; Summary and Conclusions p.17

summary.text: He argued that subcapital fractures share one basic pattern and that their differing radiographic appearance is mainly the degree of displacement. He said intermediary types may sometimes be recognised between the stages.

locator.section: Figs 6-9 captions (PDF pp.5-6)

summary.text: The stages are told apart by the position of the capital fragment and the direction of the medial weight-bearing trabeculae: distal against capital fragment in Stage I, the tilted head in Stage III, and alignment with the pelvis in Stage IV (Figs 6 to 9).

locator.section: Classification; Summary and Conclusions pp.16-17

summary.text: The paper is a 1961 report of low-angle nail fixation in 80 subcapital fractures. It proposes the classification 'in the hope that it may prove to be of additional value'. It gives no management recommendation and no outcome or prognosis data per stage.

entry.purpose: Grades the severity of osteoarthritis on radiographs of the hand, wrist, spinal apophyseal joints, hip and knee. Developed for reading x-rays in a population survey of rheumatic disease.

locator.section: Methods

definitions.text: Grade 0, none: a definite absence of x-ray changes of osteo-arthrosis.

locator.section: Intra-Observer Error (grade 1 described as minimal or doubtful); Methods grade list p.1

definitions.text: Grade 1, doubtful: the paper gives no wording beyond the label (its text on p.6 calls it minimal or doubtful). It is not counted as definite osteo-arthrosis, which the paper takes as grades 2 to 4. Standard example films are shown.

locator.section: Methods

definitions.text: Grade 2, minimal: osteo-arthrosis in the authors' opinion definitely present, though minimal in severity.

locator.section: Methods; Figs 1-8

definitions.text: Grade 3, moderate: the paper gives no wording beyond the label; standard example films are shown.

locator.section: Methods; Figs 1-8

definitions.text: Grade 4, severe: the paper gives no wording beyond the label; standard example films are shown.

locator.section: Methods

definitions.text: Features taken as evidence of osteo-arthrosis: osteophytes on the joint margins (in the knee, also on the tibial spines); periarticular ossicles, chiefly at the interphalangeal joints; cartilage narrowing with subchondral sclerosis; small pseudocystic areas with sclerotic walls, usually subchondral; altered shape of the bone ends, particularly the femoral head.

locator.section: Methods

definitions.text: For a group of joints the grade is that of the most affected joint. Where each knee was graded separately, the worse knee was used in the results.

locator.section: Inter-Observer Error

definitions.text: In this study, grades 2 to 4 counted as definite osteo-arthrosis.

locator.section: Methods; Figs 1-8

pitfalls.text: The 1957 paper does not give a written definition of grades 1, 3 and 4. Do not add criteria (for example a joint-space narrowing description) that are not in this paper.
The paper gives no management, treatment or prognosis for any grade.

locator.section: Conclusions; Summary; correlation coefficients pp.4, 6

pitfalls.text: Observers differed: inter-observer correlation was significant in all joints except the wrist, ranging from 0.10 (wrist) to 0.83 (knee; hip only 0.40), and one observer read four times as much definite hip osteo-arthrosis. Deviations of up to about +-31 per cent from the mean prevalence may be expected between observers, against about +-5 per cent for one observer reading twice (intra-observer correlation up to 0.88). The authors recommend one reader for all films or two readers in consultation.

locator.section: Inter-Observer Error, continued to p.4

pitfalls.text: For the wrist, agreement between observers was so slight it might be due to chance, chiefly when severe rheumatoid arthritis was also present.

locator.section: Introduction

pitfalls.text: In the spine, only degenerative disease of the apophyseal joints was graded. Vertebral body spur formation and disc narrowing were not included.

locator.section: Introduction

pitfalls.text: Degenerative change in synchondroses was not included. Local and primary generalized forms were not separated, nor forms secondary to trauma.

locator.section: Methods

pitfalls.text: Each joint was graded from a single view. No standard example films were shown for the lumbar spine.

locator.section: Methods

summary.text: Kellgren and Lawrence graded radiographic osteo-arthrosis on a five-point scale: none (0), doubtful (1), minimal (2), moderate (3) and severe (4).

locator.section: Methods; Figs 1-8

summary.text: The paper names the radiographic features taken as evidence of osteo-arthrosis and shows standard example films for grades 1 to 4 in most joints studied. It does not give written criteria for each grade, and it gives no management or prognosis for any grade.

locator.section: Methods p.1 (group rule); Inter-Observer Error p.3 (grades 2-4 definite)

summary.text: Grades 2 to 4 were counted as definite osteo-arthrosis; grade 1 (doubtful) was not. A group of joints, such as the distal interphalangeal joints, took the grade of its most affected joint.

locator.section: Conclusions

summary.text: The study found that different observers could grade the same films differently, enough to change prevalence estimates substantially. This rests on one small sample (85 people aged 55 to 64 from one Lancashire population, two observers), so the figures are not general.

entry.purpose: Stages the extent of chronic rhinosinusitis on CT of the paranasal sinuses, for assessing disease extent and guiding clinical management.

locator.section: Outline of staging system, paragraph 2 (journal p183)

definitions.text: Sinus group grade, scored for each of maxillary, anterior ethmoid, posterior ethmoid, sphenoid and frontal: 0 no abnormality; 1 partial opacification; 2 total opacification.

locator.section: Outline of staging system, paragraph 2 (journal p183)

definitions.text: Ostiomeatal complex (OMC): 0 if not obstructed, 2 if obstructed. No intermediate score of 1.

locator.section: Outline of staging system, paragraph 2 (journal p183)

definitions.text: Total score: sum of the sinus group grades and the OMC score, 0 to 24 overall or 0 to 12 for each side taken separately.

locator.section: Outline paragraph 2 (journal p183); Table 1 anatomic variants (p184)

definitions.text: Anatomic variants noted present (1) or absent (0) and not added to the score: absent frontal sinus, concha bullosa, paradoxical middle turbinate, Haller cells, everted uncinate process, agger nasi pneumatization.

locator.section: Table 1: Radiological grading block (journal p184)

definitions.text: Table 1 records the sinus grades and the OMC separately for the right (R) and left (L) side.

locator.section: Outline of staging system and Table 1 (journal pp183-184)

pitfalls.text: The paper defines no severity bands, thresholds or management for any total. Library note: a report should state the score (and sides) rather than label it mild, moderate or severe on this paper's authority.

locator.section: Outline paragraph 3 (journal p183)

pitfalls.text: Partial opacification is a single grade (1), whatever its extent, particularly in the maxillary sinus. The authors accept this loss of detail for ease of use and say it may be revised.

locator.section: Discussion (journal p184)

pitfalls.text: The system can over-state disease extent where secretion rather than mucosal disease produces the opacification.

locator.section: Table 1: Radiological grading, and Outline paragraph 2 (journal pp183-184)

pitfalls.text: The OMC takes only 0 or 2, never 1. The prose says only 'each sinus group'; the list of five groups (anterior and posterior ethmoids separate) comes from Table 1, so each side has five groups plus the OMC.

locator.section: Outline paragraphs 2 to 5 (journal pp183-184); Table 1

pitfalls.text: The text states endoscopic appearances are not in the staging system. Variants are stated not to score. The surgical score (own 0 to 14 total) and patient symptom score are separate sections of the form, so we read them as outside the radiological score (inference).

locator.section: Introduction (journal p183)

pitfalls.text: Developed to stage non-neoplastic sinus disease, chiefly chronic rhinosinusitis in patients undergoing endoscopic sinus surgery. The paper was not developed for tumours; it speaks of staging non-neoplastic sinus disease.

locator.section: Outline paragraph 3 (journal p183) and Discussion (p184)

pitfalls.text: The only agreement figure is a 98% correlation of scores between two people (one an author) scoring 200 scans independently; there is no validation against symptoms or outcome. The authors describe the system as a starting point open to modification.

locator.section: Outline of staging system (journal p183) and Table 1 (p184), by absence

pitfalls.text: The paper is silent on: how to score an absent or hypoplastic sinus (absent frontal sinus is listed only as a variant); what separates partial from total opacification; what counts as ostiomeatal complex obstruction; and whether post-operative anatomy is scored. The card adds no convention.

summary.text: A simple CT staging system for chronic rhinosinusitis: five sinus groups on each side are graded 0 (no abnormality), 1 (partial opacification) or 2 (total opacification).

summary.text: The ostiomeatal complex is scored 0 (not obstructed) or 2 (obstructed). The total is 0 to 24, and each side can be taken separately (0 to 12).

summary.text: The authors kept the system deliberately simple. All degrees of partial opacification share one grade, and simplicity may over-state disease extent where secretion rather than mucosal disease causes opacification.

Perfect reduction is essential; as for type III, delayed reduction is preferable to leaving the intra-articular fragment displaced. Unless undisplaced, open reduction is always necessary. If metal fixation is needed, preferably across the metaphysis; fine smooth Kirschner wires across the plate for a few weeks do not interfere with growth.
Weight-bearing must be avoided for three weeks in the hope of preventing the almost inevitable premature cessation of growth (the paper's wording).

entry.purpose: Scores spinal instability caused by a neoplastic (e.g. metastatic) spinal lesion from clinical and imaging criteria, to help identify patients with spinal tumours who may benefit from surgical consultation.

definitions.text: Spine location: junctional (occiput to C2, C7 to T2, T11 to L1, L5 to S1) 3; mobile (C3 to C6, L2 to L4) 2; semi-rigid (T3 to T10) 1; rigid (S2 to S5) 0.

locator.section: Table 3 and Mechanical Pain text (journal E1224)

definitions.text: Pain: pain with movement, upright posture or loading of the spine, and/or relieved by recumbency, 3; occasional pain that is not mechanical 1; pain-free lesion 0.

locator.section: Table 4 and Bone Lesion Quality text (journal E1224)

definitions.text: Bone lesion quality: lytic 2; mixed lytic/blastic 1; blastic 0. The authors note CT is the best modality for defining this.

locator.section: Table 5 and Spinal Alignment text (journal E1224)

definitions.text: Radiographic alignment of the motion segments affected by tumour: subluxation or translation 4; de novo kyphosis or scoliosis 2; normal 0. De novo deformity needs prior imaging or upright versus supine comparison.

locator.section: Table 6 and Vertebral Body Collapse text (journal E1224)

definitions.text: Vertebral body collapse: more than 50% collapse 3; less than 50% collapse 2; no collapse but more than 50% of the body involved 1; none of these 0.

locator.section: Table 7 and Posterolateral Involvement text (journal E1224-E1225)

definitions.text: Posterolateral involvement (facet, pedicle or costovertebral joint fracture or replacement by tumour): bilateral 3; unilateral 1; none 0.

definitions.text: Total SINS is the sum of the six component scores; the text gives a range of 0 to 18.

locator.section: Discussion: definition of spine instability (journal E1226-E1227)

definitions.text: Authors' working definition: loss of spinal integrity from a neoplastic process, associated with movement-related pain, symptomatic or progressive deformity and/or neural compromise under physiologic loads.

locator.section: Scoring paragraph versus Case 1 and Case 2 (PDF p4-p5)

pitfalls.text: At a total of 14 the paper is inconsistent: the band text labels 13 to 18 instability and case 2 (14) is unstable, but case 1 (also 14) is read as indeterminate instability. Both 14s sit in the 13 to 18 band; this pack follows the band text.

locator.section: Discussion: 'minimum score of 2 and a maximum score of 18' (journal E1228)

pitfalls.text: The scoring paragraph gives a minimum of 0; the Discussion says a minimum of 2. Component tables allow 0 for every component, so 0 is possible.

locator.section: Discussion (journal E1228)

pitfalls.text: Not summed across lesions: each lesion or region is scored separately. The score gives no global spinal score and does not predict interaction between multiple lesions.

locator.section: Discussion and Conclusion (journal E1228-E1229)

pitfalls.text: Not a decision rule on its own. With neurological deficit or high-grade cord compression surgery is indicated regardless of score; histology, prognosis, health, neurology and patient choice also bear on treatment.

locator.section: Discussion (journal E1228)

pitfalls.text: Not scored: contiguous multilevel and noncontiguous disease, prior laminectomy or surgery, prior radiation, diffuse bony involvement or poor bone quality, body weight and activity level. The authors say these are qualifiers.

locator.section: Table 6 (journal E1224)

pitfalls.text: Vertebral body collapse of exactly 50% is not defined (more than 50% scores 3, less than 50% scores 2). Table 6 scores 'none of the above' as 0 while the text scores 0 only for no body involvement, so involvement of 50% or less without collapse is not explicitly scored.

locator.section: Table 5 and Spinal Alignment text (journal E1224)

pitfalls.text: De novo deformity needs knowledge of prior imaging or upright versus supine radiographs; alignment is judged between the motion segments affected by tumour.

locator.section: Table 2: SINS component score for spine location

pitfalls.text: Rigid segments are S2 to S5 in Table 2 but S2 to S4 in its footnote.

locator.section: Conclusion (journal E1229)

pitfalls.text: Authors describe content validity from a Delphi consensus and say further validation and reliability testing are needed.

locator.section: 1.9 Tools for assessing spinal stability and prognosis, recommendations 1.9.1 and 1.9.3

pitfalls.text: NG234 recommends SINS only as a 'consider' option alongside clinical assessment and attaches no action to a score band. Its surgery recommendations are also 'consider' options within a multidisciplinary treatment plan (1.11.1, 1.11.7), unlike the paper's 'indicated regardless of score'. The 7 to 18 surgical consultation line is the paper's, not NICE's.

locator.section: Bone Lesion Quality text versus Table 4 (journal E1224)

pitfalls.text: The Bone Lesion Quality text says blastic lesions score 1 and lytic 2 with no mixed category; Tables 4 and 8 give blastic 0, mixed 1, lytic 2. The pack follows the tables.

locator.section: Scoring paragraph: sum of six component scores (journal E1224)

pitfalls.text: SINS totals are whole numbers, but the schema has no integer constraint on the input, so a fractional total such as 6.5 would band into 7 to 12. Dictate and read only whole totals.

locator.section: Scoring paragraph after Table 7: sum of 6 components, 0 to 18, bands and surgical consultation (journal E1224)

summary.text: Six components (location, pain, bone lesion quality, alignment, vertebral body collapse, posterolateral involvement) are scored and summed to give 0 to 18 for a neoplastic spinal lesion.

locator.section: Scoring paragraph after Table 7: sum of 6 components, 0 to 18, bands and surgical consultation (journal E1224)

summary.text: Bands: 0 to 6 stability; 7 to 12 indeterminate (possibly impending) instability; 13 to 18 instability. Scores of 7 to 18 warrant surgical consultation.

locator.section: Discussion (journal E1228-E1229)

summary.text: The authors stress SINS is one component of the work-up. Surgery is indicated regardless of score with neurological deficit or high-grade cord compression; modifying factors it omits must also be weighed.

locator.section: Discussion and Conclusion (journal E1228-E1229)

summary.text: Each lesion or region is scored separately; scores are not summed across lesions. The authors call for further validation and reliability testing of the score.

locator.section: 1.9 Tools for assessing spinal stability and prognosis, recommendations 1.9.1 and 1.9.3

summary.text: NICE NG234 (2023) says to consider a validated spinal stability scoring system such as SINS alongside clinical assessment, and to use scoring only within a full clinical assessment. It gives no SINS score thresholds.

locator.section: 1.5 Imaging investigations, recommendation 1.5.10

summary.text: NG234 also says to consider multiplanar viewing or 3-plane reconstruction of recent or new CT in spinal metastases or MSCC to assess spinal stability and plan vertebroplasty, kyphoplasty or spinal surgery.

entry.purpose: Grades abnormal meniscal signal on knee MRI, correlated with histological degeneration and tears. Derived from an autopsy and amputation specimen study.

locator.section: Materials and Methods: MR grading system (journal p731-732; grade 1 on p731, grades 2 and 3 continue on p732)

definitions.text: MR grade 1: one or several punctate foci of signal that do not contact an articular surface. The capsular margin of the meniscus is not counted as an articular surface.

locator.section: Materials and Methods: MR grading system (journal p731-732; grade 1 on p731, grades 2 and 3 continue on p732)

definitions.text: MR grade 2: linear intrameniscal signal that does not extend to an articular surface.

locator.section: Materials and Methods: MR grading system (journal p731-732; grade 1 on p731, grades 2 and 3 continue on p732)

definitions.text: MR grade 3: signal that extends to at least one articular surface.

locator.section: Materials and Methods: histologic stages 0-3 (journal p732)

definitions.text: Histologic stage 0: normal meniscus, intact fibrocartilaginous matrix with chondrocytes spread evenly through homogeneous collagen-reinforced ground substance.

locator.section: Materials and Methods: histologic stages 0-3 (journal p732)

definitions.text: Histologic stage 1: pale, hyponuclear foci with discrete foci of mucinous degeneration of chondrocytes. Corresponded to MR grade 1 in all 11 stage 1 segments.

locator.section: Materials and Methods: histologic stages 0-3 (journal p732)

definitions.text: Histologic stage 2: progression to discrete bands of mucinous degeneration, with no distinct cleavage plane. Corresponded to MR grade 2 in all 16 stage 2 segments.

locator.section: Materials and Methods: histologic stages 0-3 (journal p732)

definitions.text: Histologic stage 3: fibrocartilaginous separation, with or without macroscopic extension to an articular surface. Corresponded to MR grade 3 in all 8 stage 3 segments.

locator.section: Materials and Methods: MR grading system and histologic stage 0 (journal p731-732)

pitfalls.text: The paper defines MR signal grades 1 to 3 only. Normal meniscus is histologic stage 0; no MR 'grade 0' is defined. A normal meniscus on a report is simply not graded here.

locator.section: Discussion (journal p733)

pitfalls.text: No management, follow-up or surgical advice is given for any grade. The authors do say presurgical MR would help find degeneration and tears the arthroscopist may not see, calling this clinically significant, and expect posterior-horn grade 2 signal may be of prognostic importance.

locator.section: Results and Discussion: stage 3 segments; confined intrasubstance cleavage tears (journal p732-733)

pitfalls.text: Grade 3 matched fibrocartilaginous separation in every segment. Two of the eight stage 3 segments were intrasubstance tears not reaching the meniscal surface, but showed mucinous degeneration contiguous with the tear and the articular surface. Grade 3 signal may thus reflect a confined degenerative cleavage tear, which can be missed at arthroscopy.

locator.section: Discussion (journal p733)

pitfalls.text: The authors cite a 6% false-positive rate, in arthroscopically detected tears, for grade 3 signal, and read it as undiagnosed confined tears. It is quoted from reference 22 (the same group's forthcoming first-44-cases accuracy study), not measured in this series.

locator.section: Discussion: potential pitfalls in MR signal interpretation (journal p734)

pitfalls.text: Linear degeneration perpendicular to the imaging plane could be undergraded as grade 1. Focal signal on contiguous images indicates more extensive degeneration.

locator.section: Discussion: potential pitfalls in MR signal interpretation (journal p734)

pitfalls.text: Small areas of fraying or fibrillation on the free edge of the meniscus might be missed on 5 mm sections.

locator.section: Discussion: potential pitfalls in MR signal interpretation (journal p734)

pitfalls.text: Two normal structures can mimic grade 3 signal: the transverse ligament joining the anterior horns, which can look like a grade 3 signal in the anterior horn of the lateral meniscus (a pseudotear seen in about 30% of clinical knee MR examinations), and the popliteus tendon sheath at the posterior horn of the lateral meniscus, which falsely appears as a grade 3 vertical tear.

locator.section: Discussion: potential pitfalls in MR signal interpretation (journal p734)

pitfalls.text: If the body of the medial meniscus cannot be seen, consider a bucket-handle tear, especially when separate meniscal fragments are seen on coronal images. The paper's example shows grade 3 signal in both anterior and posterior horns.

locator.section: Materials and Methods (journal p731)

pitfalls.text: Grades were validated against histology in 12 menisci from older subjects (50 to 89 years), ex vivo, at 1.5 T, using sagittal 5 mm spin echo with a 800/25 sequence. Library inference, not paper text: other sequences, field strengths, younger or acutely injured knees are not addressed.

locator.section: Results and Discussion: correspondence of MR grade and histologic stage; blind protocol (journal p732-733)

pitfalls.text: The 100% match is histologic correlation of graded segments: 35 abnormal segments from 12 menisci (segments of one meniscus are not independent), read blind by two radiologists and two pathologists, ex vivo. The paper gives no inter-observer statistic, sensitivity or specificity, and does not report the MR grade of the one remaining (implied stage 0) segment. It is not diagnostic accuracy.

locator.section: Discussion: limits of arthroscopy (journal p733)

pitfalls.text: Arthroscopy could not show stage 1 and 2 degeneration, the precursors of a visible tear, and is limited for inferior, peripheral and posterior abnormalities. Stage 3 confined tears may be overlooked at arthroscopy.

locator.section: Materials and Methods: MR grading system (journal p731-732; grade 1 on p731, grades 2 and 3 continue on p732)

summary.text: Three grades of meniscal MR signal (1 to 3) defined by where the signal lies relative to an articular surface: punctate, linear intrameniscal, or reaching at least one articular surface. Read on sagittal images, corroborated on coronal.

locator.section: Results: one-to-one correspondence of MR grade and histologic stage (journal p732)

summary.text: In 12 post-mortem or amputation menisci (36 segments) each grade matched one histologic stage (grade 1 to stage 1, 2 to 2, 3 to 3) in 100% of segments; stage 3 is fibrocartilaginous separation, a tear.

locator.section: Discussion: stage 1 and 2 degeneration as potential precursors of tears (journal p733)

summary.text: The authors read stages 1 and 2 as a continuum of degeneration that ends in stage 3 tears. They suggest posterior-horn grade 2 signal may be of prognostic importance, as an expectation rather than a finding. The paper gives no management for any grade.

locator.section: Materials and Methods (journal p731)

summary.text: Ex vivo series: 12 menisci from 8 autopsies and 4 above-knee amputations, ages 50 to 89, imaged at 1.5 T with spin echo TR/TE 800/25 and 5 mm sagittal sections. Authors expect isolated MR-histology discrepancies in a larger series.
